name: Inflection of the ending (iʿrāb)
definition: The change at the end of a word caused by the governors (ʿawāmil) that enter on it, whether the change is heard or only assumed.
body: In جَاءَ زَيْدٌ (Zayd came), رَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا (I saw Zayd) and مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ (I passed by Zayd), the same word ends in -un, -an and -in. Each time another word governs it: the verb as its doer, the verb as its object, the particle bi-.
Al-Ājurrūmiyya defines iʿrāb as the change of the endings of words because of the different governors that enter on them, in pronunciation or by assumption. A word that changes in this way is muʿrab.

examples.arabic: الإِعْرَابُ هُوَ تَغْيِيرُ أَوَاخِرِ الكَلِمِ لِاخْتِلَافِ العَوَامِلِ الدَّاخِلَةِ عَلَيْهَا لَفْظًا أَوْ تَقْدِيرًا
examples.text: Iʿrāb is the change of the endings of words because of the different governors that enter on them, in pronunciation or by assumption (al-Ājurrūmiyya).
Zaydun after a verb as its doer, Zaydan as its object.
